# requireNonUndefined

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not `undefined`.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonUndefined() — Returns the value after checking that it is not `undefined`. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonUndefined<T>(
  value: T | undefined,
  message: string = "Expected a defined value."
): T;
```

The test is `typeof value === "undefined"`, which is safe for a variable that was never declared, unlike a bare comparison.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                              | Type             | Description                                                   |
| :----------------------------------------------------- | :--------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                | `T \| undefined` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a defined value."` | `string`         | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with `undefined` excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                 |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------ |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is `undefined`. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonUndefined(null); // => null
requireNonUndefined(0); // => 0
requireNonUndefined(undefined); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
